title: Open Values Entity v0.1
description: One option inside a facts file, such as a bank or a shampoo: its name, its scores from 0 to 100 on the file's criteria, and the source for each score. A score that is missing is unknown, not 0.

code.description: The entry's id, unique inside its facts file and stable over time, so other files can point at it. For food and beauty items it is the product barcode.

name.description: The name shown to people, such as "Triodos Bank".

brand.description: The brand or maker, or a short kind label where there is no brand, such as "ethical bank".

description.description: One or two plain sentences saying what the entry is.

scores.description: The entry's score on each criterion of the facts file, from 0 to 100, keyed by the criterion's key. A criterion that is missing is unknown, not 0. Every key must be declared in the file's criteria.

provenance.description: How each score is known, keyed by the same criterion keys as scores. Each value is either a short note or a citation with note, source link and date.

links.description: Links about the entry, such as its own website, each with a label and a URL.

region.description: Where the entry is available: US, UK, EU, or global. The app's region filter keeps entries for the chosen region plus the global ones.

focuses.description: Plain labels the entry carries, such as "Vegan", "Fair Trade" or "B Corp". The app matches them against the diet and preference rules a person has set, and searches them.

allergens.description: Allergen tags the product contains or may carry traces of, such as "milk" or "gluten". They come from the product's source data and, where that has none, from a keyword scan of the ingredients. An empty list does not mean the product is free of allergens.

allergensDeclared.description: True when the product's source data declares its allergens. False means there was no declared allergen data, so the allergens list may be incomplete and a reader should check the label.

label.description: The link text shown to people, such as "Website".

url.description: The address the link goes to.
